alternative_explanations: Stable opaque sensor codes still provide equality and dictionary keys, so this may test causal ordering over symbols rather than representation learning from raw perception.
Nested intervention effect sets make target discovery algorithmically privileged and may encode the chain assumption.
The raw episode predictor may be too weak; an expressive dense nonlinear model could compose interventions better at higher fit cost.
confounds: The world is a visible deterministic XOR chain with independent distractor roots, structured missingness, no measurement noise and one quick seed.
K deliberately increases both irrelevant latent roots and raw observation length, so a positive K slope measures the declared full input boundary rather than local causal execution alone.
falsification_criteria: Kill the current learned factorization if any cell has accuracy or OOD intervention accuracy below 0.90, target mapping or active-chain structure accuracy below 0.95, or capability improves by less than 0.20 over the raw episode predictor.

Reject a full-system near-zero-K claim if learned-factorized knowledge-compute slope exceeds 0.25 after charging unordered observation parsing, even when local dynamics execution remains path-bounded.

outcome_policy.negative: Learned and oracle-representation factorization fail the partially observed unknown-target task or do not beat raw prediction; discard this transfer implementation and substantially reduce HYP-0008 without benchmark patching.
outcome_policy.null: Only oracle representation remains exact or learned factorization loses its cost advantage after parsing; reduce confidence that the prior causal result transfers beyond explicit latent IDs.
outcome_policy.positive: Unknown target and sensor-level causal structure were recovered sufficiently for exact unseen intervention composition; retain the transfer mechanism but report the positive K slope from perception and require a stronger multi-seed representation test.

predicted_outcome: Learned factorized, oracle-representation and full-oracle candidates reach at least 0.95 overall and unseen paired-intervention accuracy in every quick cell; learned factorized recovers all opaque intervention targets and active-chain parent relations. The raw episode predictor stays at or below 0.75. Because every query is an unordered partial observation whose size grows with K, learned-factorized query K slope is predicted between 0.55 and 0.95 rather than zero, while its K=32 query operations are at least 80% below raw episode search. Oracle representation lowers fit cost but does not remove charged raw-observation parsing.
promotion_criteria: Quick cannot promote HYP-0008. A later transfer screen is justified only if the learned factorized candidate is exact, recovers unknown targets and structure, beats the black-box capability-cost frontier, survives multiple seeds, and does not conceal perception or routing work; positive local dynamics alone is insufficient.
research_question: After removing latent variable IDs, intervention-target labels and complete ordered state, can learned causal factorization still predict unseen paired interventions more accurately and cheaply than a raw black-box episode predictor once observation parsing and routing are fully charged?
title: Latent causal transfer with unknown sensors and intervention targets
